adjudications.topic: (a) The namespace ships both «سائن اِن» and «لاگ اِن»; the title family chose «سائن اِن» — consistent or confusing?
adjudications.verdict: PASS — consistent; سائن اِن is the term this family requires
adjudications.reasoning: Counted, not assumed: in mobile.setup, 6 pre-existing keys use سائن اِن (title_login, login, complete, complete_tui, login_tui, identity_unavailable) and exactly 1 uses لاگ اِن (owner_missing). With these three keys the namespace is 9:1 for سائن اِن, and every key that names the sign-in as a product noun — including every title — is سائن اِن. A title that used لاگ اِن would be the odd one out, so choosing سائن اِن is what consistency demands. The single لاگ اِن is not arbitrary either: it names the borrowed command-noun domain of `lop login-status`, the same register cli.login_help uses for the `lop login` command's own help. Both are ordinary Urdu; the split follows sense, not accident. Confusing? No — a reader meets سائن اِن ten times and لاگ اِن once, in a string about a command literally called `login`.

adjudications.topic: (b) «نیا/نئے» for 'newer' while the same file uses «تازہ» for 'fresh' (quotes, prices) — is that split right?
adjudications.verdict: PASS — the split is right, and it is the file's own established one
adjudications.reasoning: تازہ in this namespace means a FRESH READING of remote state: quote_unread تازہ اکاؤنٹ اور قیمت (a re-read account and price) and account_failed تازہ توثیق (a fresh re-verification); catalogue-wide it is also 'latest' (تازہ ترین). نیا means a new OBJECT or build: cloudflared … یا نیا ورژن, relay.chrome.list.new نیا. The referent of 'newer' here is a local credential row — an object that exists on disk — so نیا/نئے is the right member of the pair. Using تازہ would say 'a freshly obtained sign-in', which drifts toward the exact misreading the copy must avoid (that the user should sign in again to get one). The translator flagged this as the one call worth an Urdu reader's confirmation; I confirm it on the sense split rather than on idiom alone.

observations_outside_this_delta: «سائن اِن» is written as two space-separated tokens (سائن + U+0020 + اِن, with the kasra inside اِن), so a hard wrap can in principle split the compound. Measured: it does not split in any of these three values at any tested terminal width (80 / 100 / 120 columns), and the same form ships in 6 pre-existing keys of this namespace, so this is the namespace's existing typography rather than something this delta introduces.
At 80 columns the repoint notice takes the same 2 rows as English and the title 1; at 120 columns Urdu's receipt (97 cells) fits one row like English's (93).

The `/mobile status|enable` notice path builds a `NoticeBlock` from an already-rendered string and passes no source provenance, so the TUI's per-string RLI/PDI projection is not applied there even though the copy is Urdu. This is pre-existing paint plumbing (`OperatorApp._system_notice` → `NoticeBlock._rows` → `wrap_cells`), affects all 79 keys of this namespace, is not introduced by this delta, and must NOT be compensated for in the copy (the ur guide forbids 'fixing' a string for a terminal). Recorded so a future bidi work item starts from the right code path.

`mobile.setup` is not a `wire.*` namespace, so these strings never reach the phone client's bundled chunks; the surfaces are the CLI/TUI notice and the desktop remedy paragraph (the desktop mirrors RTL at the app root, which is a UI-repo concern).

findings.issue: This namespace ships two words for 'sign-in': سائن اِن and لاگ اِن. Both are correct Urdu; two spellings in one namespace is the kind of drift a reader notices.
findings.assessment: Not drift, and the choice is the consistent one. Counted in this tree: 6 pre-existing mobile.setup keys use سائن اِن (title_login, login, complete, complete_tui, login_tui, identity_unavailable) and exactly 1 uses لاگ اِن (owner_missing) — with these three keys the namespace is 9:1 for سائن اِن. Every title and every login key is سائن اِن, and these three join the title family, so سائن اِن is required by consistency rather than merely permitted. The lone لاگ اِن sits in the one string about `lop login-status`, where the borrowed command-name register applies (the same pattern as cli.login_help, which uses لاگ اِن for the `lop login` command's own help). It is pre-existing and outside this delta. See adjudication (a).

findings.string: نئے سائن اِن / ایک نیا سائن اِن
findings.issue: The same file uses تازہ for 'fresh' (`quote_unread`: تازہ اکاؤنٹ اور قیمت, `account_failed`: تازہ توثیق) while the new keys use نیا / نئے for 'newer'. A reader could ask why the same domain uses two adjectives for near-neighbours.
findings.assessment: The split is deliberate and correct, and it is the file's own. تازہ is this namespace's word for a FRESH READING of remote state — a re-read price, a re-verified account — and across the catalogue for 'latest' (تازہ ترین). نیا is its word for a new OBJECT or build (cloudflared … یا نیا ورژن). The referent here is a local credential row: an object, not a reading. Using تازہ would say 'a freshly obtained sign-in', which is uncomfortably close to the one reading the copy must avoid ('sign in again'). See adjudication (b).

findings.status: accepted — no change; recorded as a wrap measurement
findings.issue: The receipt is 97 rendered cells against the English source's 93. At the TUI notice's real body width for a 100-column terminal (94 cells) the English receipt fits one row while this one wraps to two, and the break falls between «(کریڈینشل» and «42)۔».
findings.assessment: Measured with the product's own `wrap_cells` at `NoticeBlock.body_budget`, not guessed. Nothing is truncated or lost, the {id} digits stay whole and in the right order, and at the default 80-column terminal both English and Urdu take two rows — so this is a difference in a narrow band of terminal widths, not a defect. Arabic script measures ≈1 cell per character and the style guide's instruction is 'keep within maxCells; prefer short'; no maxCells is declared for these keys, and the receipt is deliberately 4 cells longer than English because Urdu needs postpositions (اسی اکاؤنٹ کے لیے) that English leaves implicit. Not worth a remediation round; recorded so the next wave can see the consequence if it shortens the receipt.
